title: Reading Drill — Mapping falling leaves on cycleways — Building a comparison
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Mapping falling leaves on cycleways — Building a comparison
passages.body:
**A** The cycleway inspector had been asked to investigate leaves collecting at bends rather than under the trees in Brackenton. Its first task was to decide which signs of improvement could be compared between sites. It settled on the area covered by leaves, because the same measure could be applied in the original setting and at a second location.

**B** During a seven-week comparison, the team used fixed camera locations at both places. It recorded outcomes separately for each site. Because wind after sunset might influence the figures, the team used a column in the record to show when that condition was present. The surveys included quiet periods as well as busy ones.

**C** The team then put forward sweeping at selected bends. Its report asked for another comparison after the change had been tried. This would distinguish a genuine effect from an improvement that could have occurred anyway. The report did not assume that the more successful site before the change would be the better site afterwards.
